pr_title: BUG: read_excel failed with empty rows after MultiIndex header
pr_body:
- [x] closes #40442
- [x] tests added / passed
- [x] Ensure all linting tests pass, see [here](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing.html#code-standards) for how to run them
- [x] whatsnew entry

Prior to this fix, a blank data row after a MultiIndex header was a interpreted as containing a blank index name, but that only works if the user has specified an index column. If index_col is None all subsequent rows should be treated as data, even if the first one is empty.
pr_comments: @jreback I've added the new comments; let me know if anything else is needed. Thanks

**Note**: Please read [this guide](https://matthewrocklin.com/blog/work/2018/02/28/minimal-bug-reports) detailing how to provide the necessary information for us to reproduce your bug.

#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example

```python
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

excel_file = Path("test_excel_file.xlsx")

```

#### Problem description

| **part 1**       | **part 2**      | **part 3**       |

```python
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test_pandas_openpyxl.py", line 12, in <module>

    assert index is not None
AssertionError
```

I suspect there are two different bugs here. The first is the crash (above), but the second is the text parser consuming one of the empty lines in this particular case:

```python
from io import StringIO
data = 'A,A,B\na,b,a\n,,\n,,\n1,2,3\n4,5,6\n7,8,9\n'
pd.read_csv(StringIO(data), header=[0,1])
```

```
     A         B
     a    b    a
0  NaN  NaN  NaN
1  1.0  2.0  3.0
2  4.0  5.0  6.0
3  7.0  8.0  9.0

```

This second bug is probably related to #34188

Thanks @neutronleak. Reproducible example:

```
df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        'a': ['A', None, None, '1', '2'],
        'b': ['B', None, None, '3', '4'],
    }
)
df.to_excel('test.xlsx', index=False)
pd.read_excel('test.xlsx', engine='openpyxl', header=[0, 1])
```

The method OpenpyxlReader.get_sheet_data is returning

     [['a', 'b'], ['A', 'B'], ['', ''], ['', ''], ['1', '3'], ['2', '4']]

which looks right to me, so I think this isn't an openpyxl-specific issue, but rather the parser. I think you're right @ahawryluk, the other issue looks related; thanks for bringing that up.

review_comments:
The docstring for TextParser says about has_index_names:

> True if the cols defined in index_col have an index name and are not in the header.

From this, it seems to me the inclusion of index_col you're doing here is correct. However I don't understand the other two conditions - can't we have index names when there is only one row for the header?

From the [0.17 changes](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/whatsnew/v0.17.0.html#changes-to-excel-with-multiindex), it appears that `has_index_names` was an argument for `read_excel` because the Excel output used to place the index name on its own row even for single-row headers. It was [dropped in 0.21](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/whatsnew/v0.17.0.html#changes-to-excel-with-multiindex). The name is a bit confusing now. Maybe `has_index_name_row` would be better, but I'd have to check carefully before attempting a change. The are 14 lines on the code with `has_index_names` and some might have different meanings than this one.

Thanks! To summarize, when header is a single row, the index names will not be on their own row. However, when header is multiple rows, the index names will be on their own row. Certainly wouldn't recommend changing the name here.
Can you add an issue comment here as well?
Can this also impact read_fwf, read_table, and maybe others?
I suspect that's true. I'll check for other formats and add tests for MultiIndex headers with no index.
I've checked the other formats, but didn't add new tests because there are existing tests in place to ensure that e.g. read_table behaves the same as read_csv without duplicating every common test.
Thanks for checking, but I don't quite follow. What tests are you referring to?

When I wrote 

> I suspect that's true. I'll check for other formats and add tests for MultiIndex headers with no index.

I thought I would need to add tests for read_table, and read_fwf, but now I see that pandas doesn't duplicate those redundant tests. Instead, tests/io contains read_csv 653 times, read_table 31 times, and read_fwf 49 times. The tests for read_table and read_fwf are just the minimum required to show that they correctly match read_csv, and read_csv is tested in more detail. So I don't think I should add any more tests for this pull request, but that's just my best guess based on what I see so far in the code. Let me know if there's anything else to improve.
